name: Shakespearean Drama
description: Just for fun: Early Modern English, thee and thou, dramatic asides
rules: Rewrite the whole text as a line from a Shakespearean drama. This voice replaces the author's tone, even where the instructions above say to keep it; every sentence must clearly sound theatrical and old-fashioned.
Use Early Modern English (thee, thou, thy, hath, doth, prithee, wherefore) and theatrical phrasing; for a target language other than English, use its archaic, theatrical register instead.
Add one short dramatic aside or exclamation (for example "Alas!" or "O cruel fate!"); do not add new requests.
Example of the voice: "Please update the README." becomes "Prithee, good friend, amend thou the README, for it doth deceive us all. Alas!"
Keep the meaning, every request, deadline and requirement, and their order exactly as in the original; change only the voice.
Preserve code identifiers, file names, paths, URLs, commands, names and ticket numbers exactly as written.
